subject: Urgent: Acme demo — realtime payload starvation causing delivery gaps (exec attention)
body:
From: Ethan Miller <ethan@acme.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime delivery gaps during demo (session id: 0x9f3b)

Hi Neha —

We ran into a pretty bad issue this morning during our internal demo using the Redwood realtime endpoint. The UI shows the model generating fine but the client sees long silent gaps (5–20s) where no chunks arrive; the connection doesn't drop immediately, it just stalls and then resumes. This happened on two consecutive sessions and is reproducible when we push concurrent requests (30-40 RPS) against the same workspace.

Attached: acme_capture_2028-07-06.log and a short trace snippet (trace_session_0x9f3b.txt).

Key details:
- Session id: 0x9f3b (attached traces)
- Observed 3 stalls in ~10 minutes; gaps varied 6s, 12s, 18s
- Clients report single TCP/TLS connection; no reconnects required to resume
- We were running a demo candidate at latency target ~200ms; these gaps make the demo unusable

Can you triage urgently? Our stakeholders are watching and we need a short-term mitigation while you debug.

—Ethan
Ethan Miller
Platform Engineer, Acme Robotics
ethan@acme.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Miller <ethan@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Jul 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime delivery gaps during demo (session id: 0x9f3b)

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Ethan — sorry you're seeing this. Looping in engineering (Jonas) and SRE (Aditya) so we can get a triage started.

Marissa — FYI this is on the Acme POC (ACME-2028-EXP-42); they're in a demo window today.

Jonas/Aditya — attached are Ethan's logs. Quick asks to prioritize triage:
- Can you confirm whether this looks like a server-side chunking/drain event vs. client-side backpressure?
- If server-side, can we identify whether the edge proxy (nginx/edge-gw) is pausing chunk flushes under certain payload patterns?
- Any quick mitigations we can apply (route pin to dedicated pool, aggressive keepalives, temporary downgrade to non-streaming mode)?

Ethan — can you also paste the full request headers and the approximate timestamps (UTC) for the three stalls? That will make correlation much faster.

I'll set up a short bridge if we need it.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ethan Miller <ethan@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime delivery gaps during demo (session id: 0x9f3b)

Thanks for the traces, Ethan. Initial read: the exporter shows continuous token generation on the model side, but the edge traces indicate that chunked-transfer flushes stop for the observed gap windows. Two hypotheses:

1) Proxy-side buffer/backpressure: when multiple long-running sessions hit the same edge worker, internal buffering combined with delayed flushes can produce periodic silence until the worker drains.
2) Kernel/serve handshake: under specific sequence-length distributions the runtime switches execution kernels that temporarily stall the KV-cache flush path. This is rare but plausible.

Immediate triage steps I'm requesting from SRE/edge team:
- Pull raw edge gateway logs for the edge-worker handling session 0x9f3b for the UTC timestamps Ethan will provide
- Check connection-level keepalive (idle) and per-chunk flush timings; look for API-level 200 responses with delayed body writes
- If we can reproduce, try pinning the session to a different pool and observe

Ethan — can you run a small synthetic with the same concurrency but single-model short prompts? That helps isolate model/kernel vs. edge behavior.

I'll be available on the bridge if useful.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 07 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime delivery gaps during demo (session id: 0x9f3b)

Thanks — added the full header dump and the timestamps (UTC) for each gap to the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1ACME-shared-triage (files: acme_capture_2028-07-07.zip).

Note: the problem got significantly worse during our all-hands yesterday (July 7). We saw consistent 10–25s blackouts across multiple users, and one of our stakeholders explicitly mentioned this as a reason they're considering switching vendors. We need an interim fix and a clear timeline for a permanent solution.

We can run the synthetic tests Jonas suggested — but given how this looks in production, we'd like exec visibility. Can someone from Redwood leadership join a quick call?

—Ethan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Miller <ethan@acme.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Jul 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime delivery gaps during demo (session id: 0x9f3b)

Ethan — appreciate the extra detail and the Drive upload. I'm escalating this immediately. I agree we need a short-term mitigation while engineering digs in. Proposed immediate actions (we can discuss on a 30m call):

- Failover the Acme workspace to a dedicated pool for the next 24h (reduces noisy-neighbor risk)
- If failover is not possible instantly, enable per-connection aggressive keepalives and reduce maximum chunk buffer on the edge (we can roll config in <2h)
- Offer Acme a service credit for the impacted demo session (TBD amount) and commit to a post-mortem w/ timeline within 72 hours

Jonas/Aditya — can you confirm whether any of these are low-risk to apply now? I can coordinate approvals.

Marissa Cole

Date: Sun, 08 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Realtime delivery gaps during demo (session id: 0x9f3b)

Executive summary and immediate plan:

- Impact: Acme reported repeated realtime delivery gaps (5–25s) during demo traffic; customer-facing impact is high and churn risk exists.
- Short-term mitigation (next 2h):
  1) Route pin Acme workspace to dedicated pool (Marissa to approve; ops to execute now)
  2) Edge keepalive/config roll: reduce chunk buffer and set per-chunk flush threshold to 50ms (SRE)
  3) Optional: enable fallback to non-streaming response for demo connections (feature flag) if streaming continues to fail
- Triage plan (24–72h):
  1) Correlate edge-worker logs with model-side token emission traces for the affected sessions (Jonas assigned)\  2) Run synthetic workload reproducer to isolate kernel vs. proxy (engineering)\  3) If kernel path implicated, prepare a hotfix to avoid kernel swap during active sessions (may require small runtime patch)
- Communication: Marissa to send customer-facing note with mitigation + offer of credit. I'll prepare internal post-mortem template and assign owners.

Owners and suggested ETA:
- Marissa: Approve dedicated pool failover (ETA: immediate)
- Ops on-call (SRE): Edge config roll (ETA: 2h)
- Jonas: Deep triage and repro (ETA: 48h preliminary)
- Aditya (SRE lead): Post-mortem + timeline (ETA: 72h)

Attachments: rwc_edge_snapshot_2028-07-07.json (edge snapshot), screenshot_lag.png

I'll join the customer call if scheduled. Neha/Marissa — please confirm the time and I'll be on the bridge.

-Aditya Rao
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
